Today, we joined Auckland Transport, Auckland One Rail and media at Karanga-a-Hape Station to view the final full City Rail Link (CRL) timetable test and rehearsal in action.

KiwiRail Chief Metro Officer Bevan Assink says this weekend’s full Auckland rail closure is expected to be the last time the network shuts before passengers can travel on the CRL.

“I can assure Aucklanders that we won’t be closing the entire network again this year, or even this summer,” Assink said. “Full network shutdowns will only happen as the exception from here.”

Following CRL practical completion, KiwiRail owns and manages its tunnels and track. 

While some parts of the network will still need to close over December and January, future works will be targeted to specific sections rather than requiring a network-wide shut down. 

The partial summer closure will be for remaining resilience and reliability upgrades – but this will be targeted and much shorter than in recent years, Assink says.

This weekend’s closure, from 10–12 July, will support rail infrastructure upgrades, level crossing improvements and today, the testing of Day 1 CRL operations. Testing today includes the weekday timetable that will be introduced when the CRL opens.

Found only in high-quality wetlands and classified as At Risk–Declining, the brown mudfish highlights the ecological importance of the area.

For more information, read our media release here: https://lnkd.in/dnEA65Mn","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/kiwirail_a-rare-brown-mudfish-known-locally-as-hauhau-activity-7479051394965200896-Fr6c"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"KiwiRail","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/kiwirail"},"datePublished":"2026-07-03T05:21:04.937Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/kiwirail_considerrail-kiwirailfreight-supplychain-activity-7478679185478180864-DOdC","text":"Who knew freight conversations could be fuelled by train-shaped cookies?

This week the KiwiRail Freight team was proud to be part of the inaugural Aka Raupapa – National Freight and Supply Chain Superhui in Hamilton, hosted by Tainui Group Holdings in partnership with Brightstar.

We set up our Consider Rail booth, had some great conversations with customers, partners and industry peers, and attracted plenty of visitors with our custom-made train cookies.

While the cookies were a hit, the real value was in bringing together leaders from across industry, iwi and Government to talk about the challenges and opportunities facing New Zealand's freight and supply chain sector. From infrastructure constraints to productivity and resilience, there was no shortage of important discussions.

A particular highlight was seeing our Chief Customer and Growth Officer, Adele Wilson, join the panel on "Reimagining New Zealand's supply chain: Productivity, resilience and prosperity for the decade ahead." Adele shared KiwiRail's perspective on the importance of connected thinking and coordinated investment across the freight network to help move more freight, more efficiently, across Aotearoa.

Thanks to everyone who stopped by the stand for a kōrero and a cookie. 

We're already looking forward to the next one.

#ConsiderRail #KiwiRailFreight #SupplyChain #Freight #Logistics #AkaRaupapa #Superhui #RailFreight #FutureOfFreight","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/kiwirail_considerrail-kiwirailfreight-supplychain-activity-7478679185478180864-DOdC"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"KiwiRail","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/kiwirail"},"datePublished":"2026-07-02T04:16:33.724Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/kiwirail_kiwirail-railfreight-supplychain-activity-7478300560601915392-l-VG","text":"Strengthening New Zealand’s supply chains through rail 

On 29 June, Palmerston North – a key North Island supply chain hub – was the focus of KiwiRail’s latest Connect event, bringing together 60 Manawatū businesses, industry partners, and customers to discuss the future of freight and the role rail can play in strengthening regional supply chains.

A key message from the evening was: Consider Rail, we have capacity to grow, and we want to work with businesses to move more freight by rail.
As one of KiwiRail’s most important freight hubs, Palmerston North sees more than 140 trains each week, connecting freight to key centres across New Zealand. Businesses in the region benefit from regular services to Auckland, Tauranga, Napier, Wellington, New Plymouth and Whanganui, along with seamless connections to major ports and the South Island.

Rail continues to play a critical role in linking producers, freight forwarders, ports and logistics providers, supporting efficient freight movement across the country. With available capacity across key corridors, there are real opportunities for businesses to optimise supply chains and reduce their transport emissions.

A big thank you to everyone who attended, including our customers, industry partners, local mayors Grant Smith (Palmerston North City Council), Michael Ford (Manawatū District Council) and Andy Watson (Rangitīkei District Council), and Jerry Shearman, Chief Executive of CEDA, for supporting this important regional conversation.

If you're looking to explore how rail could support your business, we'd love to continue the conversation contact - salesquotes@kiwirail.co.nz

The number of substations around the Wellington region is growing by five as KiwiRail gets the Wellington Metro ready for faster, more frequent services.   
  
Demand on the overhead line by trains is going to increase substantially with more trains, so it’s time to bolster the overhead line voltage to allow for that.    
  
The new substations will supply power equivalent to over 1,000 homes! 
  
Thanks to Government funding for the project, work to install the substations is well underway in several locations.   
  
It’s a complex but rewarding project that will make a big difference to the regions public transport.

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Final City Rail Link full rehearsal tests network readiness

Today, we joined <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/auckland-transport?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Auckland Transport</a>, <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/auckland-one-rail?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Auckland One Rail</a> and media at Karanga-a-Hape Station to view the final full City Rail Link (CRL) timetable test and rehearsal in action.

KiwiRail Chief Metro Officer <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/bevan-assink-83bb3930?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Bevan Assink</a> says this weekend’s full Auckland rail closure is expected to be the last time the network shuts before passengers can travel on the CRL.

“I can assure Aucklanders that we won’t be closing the entire network again this year, or even this summer,” Assink said. “Full network shutdowns will only happen as the exception from here.”

Following CRL practical completion, KiwiRail owns and manages its tunnels and track. 

While some parts of the network will still need to close over December and January, future works will be targeted to specific sections rather than requiring a network-wide shut down. 

The partial summer closure will be for remaining resilience and reliability upgrades – but this will be targeted and much shorter than in recent years, Assink says.

This weekend’s closure, from 10–12 July, will support rail infrastructure upgrades, level crossing improvements and today, the testing of Day 1 CRL operations. Testing today includes the weekday timetable that will be introduced when the CRL opens.

“We’re excited to see the benefits once the City Rail Link opens later this year, alongside the two new railway stations in Drury which passengers will be able to use in the coming months.”</p>

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">A rare brown mudfish, known locally as hauhau, was a welcome find for our team while clearing culverts in Koputaroa last month.
 
The mudfish was discovered during a fish rescue and relocation operation carried out alongside Wildlands ecologists and local contractors, with a total of 36 fish safely relocated before work began.
 
Found only in high-quality wetlands and classified as At Risk–Declining, the brown mudfish highlights the ecological importance of the area.
 
Looking after wetlands and the environment we work in is an important part of the work to prepare the Manawatū Line for faster and more frequent rail services.

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Who knew freight conversations could be fuelled by train-shaped cookies?

This week the KiwiRail Freight team was proud to be part of the inaugural Aka Raupapa – National Freight and Supply Chain Superhui in Hamilton, hosted by Tainui Group Holdings in partnership with Brightstar.

We set up our Consider Rail booth, had some great conversations with customers, partners and industry peers, and attracted plenty of visitors with our custom-made train cookies.

While the cookies were a hit, the real value was in bringing together leaders from across industry, iwi and Government to talk about the challenges and opportunities facing New Zealand's freight and supply chain sector. From infrastructure constraints to productivity and resilience, there was no shortage of important discussions.

A particular highlight was seeing our Chief Customer and Growth Officer, <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/adele-wilson-01784178?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Adele Wilson</a>, join the panel on "Reimagining New Zealand's supply chain: Productivity, resilience and prosperity for the decade ahead." Adele shared KiwiRail's perspective on the importance of connected thinking and coordinated investment across the freight network to help move more freight, more efficiently, across Aotearoa.

Thanks to everyone who stopped by the stand for a kōrero and a cookie. 

We're already looking forward to the next one.

        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Strengthening New Zealand’s supply chains through rail 

On 29 June, Palmerston North – a key North Island supply chain hub – was the focus of KiwiRail’s latest Connect event, bringing together 60 Manawatū businesses, industry partners, and customers to discuss the future of freight and the role rail can play in strengthening regional supply chains.

A key message from the evening was: Consider Rail, we have capacity to grow, and we want to work with businesses to move more freight by rail.
As one of KiwiRail’s most important freight hubs, Palmerston North sees more than 140 trains each week, connecting freight to key centres across New Zealand. Businesses in the region benefit from regular services to Auckland, Tauranga, Napier, Wellington, New Plymouth and Whanganui, along with seamless connections to major ports and the South Island.

Rail continues to play a critical role in linking producers, freight forwarders, ports and logistics providers, supporting efficient freight movement across the country. With available capacity across key corridors, there are real opportunities for businesses to optimise supply chains and reduce their transport emissions.

A big thank you to everyone who attended, including our customers, industry partners, local mayors Grant Smith (Palmerston North City Council), Michael Ford (Manawatū District Council) and Andy Watson (Rangitīkei District Council), and Jerry Shearman, Chief Executive of CEDA, for supporting this important regional conversation.
